title: Security Evaluation Models
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 3: Security Architecture and Engineering: Security Evaluation Models.

items: Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria (U.S. DoD, 1985)
Evaluates confidentiality only (no integrity or availability)
Levels: D (minimal) → C1, C2 (discretionary) → B1, B2, B3 (mandatory) → A1 (verified)
Part of the Rainbow Series of security publications
Replaced by Common Criteria but still historically important for CISSP

rows: Object reuse protection; auditing (e.g., Windows NT)

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: TCSEC evaluates CONFIDENTIALITY only. ITSEC (European) was the first to add integrity and availability evaluation.

items: ISO/IEC 15408 — International standard for IT security evaluation
Protection Profile (PP) — Describes security requirements for a category of products
Security Target (ST) — Vendor's claim of what their product does
Evaluation Assurance Level (EAL) — EAL1 (lowest) to EAL7 (highest)

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: EAL4 is the highest level that is typically commercially achievable. EAL5-EAL7 require formal methods and are rarely achieved by commercial products.
